title: Second commandment (CCC 2142–2159)
hookLine: the holy name, and your own name too

lines: A NAME MISSPELLED ON A CUP.
A FULL NAME READ AT A FUNERAL.
cards: The coffee shop is loud. The barista slides a cup across the counter and calls out a name that's almost yours, spelled the way no one has ever spelled it.
Later that week, at a funeral, a grandson reads his grandmother's full name aloud, every part of it, slowly, and the room goes still.
Same thing, a name: in one place scribbled and forgotten, in the other held like something precious. Today's commandment is about a name, God's, and it ends up being about yours.

teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain." The Catechism begins with a gift: God entrusts his name to those who believe in him, as he told Moses his name at the burning bush.
To give someone your name is to let them call on you. So the commandment asks for the respect you'd give the name of someone you love. Then it names what goes against it.

teach.h: NOT IN VAIN: BLASPHEMY, FALSE OATHS.
teach.b: Blasphemy: words of hatred or contempt aimed at God, the Church or the saints. Using God's name to cover crimes, or to justify violence against a people. Careless swearing, where the holiest name becomes filler.
And a false oath: calling on God as witness to a lie. Jesus goes further in the Sermon on the Mount: don't swear at all; let your yes mean yes.

The Church still allows an oath for a serious and just reason, like testimony in court. A person is baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and receives their own name in the Church.

teach.h: GOD CALLS EACH ONE BY NAME.
teach.b: God calls each one by name, the Catechism says, and everyone's name is sacred: the icon of the person, a sign of the dignity of the one who bears it.

teach.h: A WHITE STONE, A NEW NAME.
teach.b: In Revelation, the one who overcomes is promised a white stone with a new name on it, known only to the one who receives it.
So the second commandment guards two names at once: the name above every name, and the one on your coffee cup.

how: Catholics are taught to speak God's name with reverence; at baptism a child receives a Christian name, which may be a saint's, and the priest baptizes in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

o: a ban on naming a child after a saint
respect for God's name, and for every name
never saying any word for God out loud

games.q: the second commandment — tap the pairs.
p: words of contempt aimed at God
calling God to witness a lie
receiving your name in the Church
a new name, known to the receiver

s: the second commandment is only about swearing
the Catechism also covers blasphemy, oaths, and the dignity of every person's name.
the Catechism calls a person's name sacred
it calls a name the icon of the person.
the Church forbids every oath, even in court
the Catechism allows an oath for a serious and just reason.

games.q: you're asked to swear before God that something is true, and it's a small lie that would spare everyone trouble. what does the second commandment say?
o: never call God to witness a lie.
games.why: the Catechism says a false oath calls on God to be witness to a lie, and calls perjury a grave lack of respect for the Lord of all speech.

practice: If you pray, say God's name once, slowly, the way you'd say the name of someone you trust, and let the silence after it be long; if you don't, say the name of someone you love just as slowly, and notice how a name carries a whole person.
Then say your own name, quietly, as though someone kind were saying it to you.

wordCard.voice: Second commandment. Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: respect for God's name, and, the Catechism adds, for every person's name. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: names are holy. God's name first, and then every other name after it. That's the day.

sources.q: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain.
